verdict.rationale: The only direct evidence is a hands-on community report of turning on Remote Management on one Mac and logging into it via Remote Desktop (macos-comm-2). That shows a built-in way to expose a Mac desktop for remote access, though it appears in the context of a security bug. First-party docs cover only adjacent nearby-device features: iPhone Mirroring lets you view and control an iPhone from the Mac, and AirPlay-style sharing shows content from another Apple device on the Mac's screen. Neither amounts to general remote desktop sharing. Missing for 10: first-party docs for Screen Sharing/Remote Management, evidence of connecting to remote non-Apple or cross-network desktop sessions, setup and security configuration details, and independent corroboration of quality and performance.
